note: The shape of a documentation page: the vocabularies its metadata may use, the sections its body must carry, and the sections of the corpus it may live in. `scripts/check-docs-pages.mjs` enforces this and the reading surface renders from it, so a status badge and the gate that judges it cannot disagree. Every vocabulary here carries a `label` a surface may print and a `note` saying what the term means; keeping the three the same shape is what stops a definition being rendered where a name belongs. A page names the domain of the directory it sits in; the few pages at the corpus root — its entrance and its glossary — are documentation about the documentation, and name `meta`.

user.label: User
user.note: Someone using Vitae to run their own career work.

designer.label: Designer
designer.note: Someone changing how a surface looks, reads or behaves.

maintainer.label: Maintainer
maintainer.note: Someone responsible for the shape of the system over time.

operator.label: Operator
operator.note: Someone deploying, migrating, backing up or recovering an instance.

security.label: Security reviewer
security.note: Someone reviewing trust boundaries, data handling or failure modes.

product.title: Product
product.summary: What Vitae is for, who it serves, and where its boundaries are.

use.title: Use
use.summary: Working the product: onboarding, tasks, every screen, and what to do when something goes wrong.

design.title: Design
design.summary: The Quiet Observatory: identity, tokens, patterns, states, motion, accessibility and voice.

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.summary: How the system is put together, from the request lifecycle down to the typed career graph.

develop.title: Develop
develop.summary: Setting up, finding where a change belongs, testing it, and shipping it safely.

operate.title: Operate
operate.summary: Running an instance: deployment, migration, backup, restore, rotation and incident response.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.summary: The architecture decisions on record, including the ones that have been replaced.

meta.title: About these documents
meta.summary: What this documentation covers, what it does not, and the rules that keep it true.

index.label: Section index
index.note: Leads a reader into a section. Carries no facts of its own that a page below it does not carry.

explanation.label: Explanation
explanation.note: Builds understanding of something that already exists.

tutorial.label: Tutorial
tutorial.note: Takes a newcomer through a first success, start to finish.

task.label: Task
task.note: Answers a specific goal someone already has.

reference.label: Reference
reference.note: States facts to be looked up, not read through.

decision.label: Decision
decision.note: Records a choice, its context and its consequences.

verified.label: Verified
verified.note: Checked against the code at the revision named in verified_at.

partial.label: Partly implemented
partial.note: Some of what this describes ships; the page says which parts do not.

planned.label: Planned
planned.note: Intent, not behaviour. Nothing here is claimed to run today.

gated.label: Gated
gated.note: Implemented but not reachable in a default build; a flag or a launch step holds it closed.

deprecated.label: Deprecated
deprecated.note: Kept so existing links resolve. Points at what replaced it.

historical.label: Historical
historical.note: True when it was written, kept as a record rather than as guidance.

generated.label: Generated
generated.note: Derived from the source by a script. Editing the page by hand will be overwritten.

needs-review.label: Needs review
needs-review.note: Reconstructed from evidence rather than from a record, and not yet confirmed by someone who would know.

app_routes_note: Paths under /docs that the application serves but no page produces — search, the glossary index, reference catalogs. Every entry must appear in docs/generated/routes.json, so this list cannot promise a destination the router does not mount.
